correctness.rationale: Explicit orthonormal Fourier diagonalization gives simple energies except flux 0 or π; an involution of energy-degenerate frequency pairs and the exact divisibility equivalence N | d(2k+m) iff M | (2k+m) produce (C_m-S_m)/2, with singleton correction. The dissipative numerical-range identity forces strict spectral decay off the reducing dark subspace, proving the asymptotic trace. The embedded finite checker passed 5,307 eigen-constraint cases, exhaustive modular checks for all N=3..120, and eight dissipative examples. No extrapolation from finite tests is used.

originality.rationale: Prior zero-flux two-node unobservability is fully covered by Parlangeli–Notarstefano, arXiv:1109.3556; this is explicitly disclosed. New mathematical content is the generic/half-flux spectral splitting, arithmetic dimension and parity-dependent switch for two absorbing sites, not implied by the checked single-trap and small-dot magnetic transport literature. Targeted published-finding corpus and primary-paper implication comparisons were completed with recorded limitations.
residual_risks: A not-yet-located signed-cycle observability study could encode the same half-flux formula.

General physical flux interferences are known for small quantum dot rings and should not themselves be claimed as new.

value.rationale: The exactly persistent population under two physically natural lossy contacts is a sharp all-size transport invariant with a substantial parity-mediated magnetic switch. The half-flux response is exactly calculable from the geometry and independent of loss rate: in one family a dark mode is created, in another all dark modes are annihilated. This is a natural benchmark for coherent transport and trap placement, not an arbitrary finite slice; the known zero-flux baseline is not used to inflate value.
